elements.element: Kubient must maintain commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: The clause requires “commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.”

elements.element: Kubient must maintain commercial general liability insurance with at least a USD 2,000,000 aggregate limit.
elements.evidence: The clause requires commercial general liability insurance of “USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.”

elements.element: Kubient must maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly requires “professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000.”

elements.element: If Kubient processes Customer Data, Kubient must maintain cyber/privacy liability insurance of at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: The condition applies because the operative language contemplates Kubient collecting, storing, processing, or accessing Customer data or visitor information; in that event, it requires “cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000.” Cyber liability is used as the applicable cyber/privacy coverage category.

elements.element: Kubient must maintain workers’ compensation insurance as required by law.
elements.evidence: The clause requires “workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable Law.”

elements.element: Kubient must provide certificates of insurance to Customer upon request.
elements.evidence: The clause states that “Kubient shall provide Customer with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage upon request.”

elements.element: Kubient must maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The required USD 1,000,000 fallback limit is exceeded by the operative USD 2,000,000 E&O requirement.

elements.element: If Kubient processes Customer Data, Kubient must maintain cyber liability insurance of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: The operative clause expressly covers collection, storage, processing, or access to Customer data and requires USD 5,000,000 of cyber liability insurance, exceeding the fallback limit.

result.reason: The operative language satisfies every preferred requirement and therefore also exceeds both fallback limits. It is not minimal because it additionally requires coverage at Kubient’s expense for one year after the Term and unnecessarily reorders the existing provisions. The insurance addition does not contradict or eliminate the unrelated operative terms, but drafting quality is reduced by the unnumbered insertion, provision reordering, inconsistent capitalization of “Customer data,” and the unnecessary post-Term requirement.
